(2009), 'Anything is Possible: On the Existence and Uniqueness of Equilibria in the Shleifer-Vishny Model of Limits of Arbitrage', Review of Finance 13(3) 521-553, DOI 10.1093/rof/rfn016 (RePEc https://ideas.repec.org/a/oup/revfin/v13y2009i3p521-553.html and OUP https://academic.oup.com/rof/article/13/3/521/1592327, both WebFetched 2026-10-23). Abstract (RePEc, paraphrased by the fetch tool): existence requires equilibrium types SV overlooked even under their parameter restrictions; outside them multiple equilibria arise with sunspots; and 'an equilibrium may exist in which the asset price returns to fundamentals even as noise trader sentiment worsens'. The 2006 working-paper version (https://epub.uni-regensburg.de/15563/1/limits_of_arbitrage.pdf, Regensburg DP 418) §3.4 'early recovery equilibria': D1 = F1 (fully invested), a > 1, misperceptions deepen, p2 = V, and F2 > D1 (Example 6: F2 = 0.7 vs D1 = 0.2; Examples 6-7 lie outside SV's p. 46 stability condition, footnote 15). That is a case meeting Proposition 3's stated hypotheses where its conclusion F2 < D1 fails, i.e. published work qualifying the very result cited. Neither page, nor card AP1-c009, names it; arnold2009 is not in the registry (grep 'Arnold' references/references.json -> 0). Note also: the page's 'when a mispricing deepens' (price falls, p2 < p1) is narrower than SV's 'misperceptions deepen', and under p2 < p1 the result is a two-line substitution - which is what option (a) would use.
